birthday.letter.friend.1: {{player}}:^^I heard today is your birthday, so I made sure to slip this letter into your mailbox this morning. I put a little something in with it too—hope you don't mind.^^Take it easy on chores today and enjoy your day.
birthday.letter.friend.2: Hey, {{player}}!^^Happy birthday! I'm not great at writing letters like this, but the point is—I'm glad someone like you is in town.^^Here's a little something from me. I hope today goes smoothly for you.
birthday.letter.friend.3: {{player}}:^^Another year older! The farm can wait until tomorrow—just take today off.^^There's a small gift in the envelope. I hope it's useful.
birthday.letter.friend.4: {{player}}, greetings:^^When I turned the calendar to today, I finally felt sure I hadn't mixed up the date. Happy birthday!^^The little thing inside isn't worth much. Tell me next time we meet whether you like it.
birthday.letter.romance.1: {{player}}:^^I meant to tell you in person, but I couldn't resist the thought of you getting it as soon as you opened your eyes—happy birthday.^^When you see what's in the envelope, think of me, okay?
birthday.letter.romance.2: Dear {{player}}:^^The first thing I thought of when I woke up today was you. Happy birthday!^^It's a small gift, but it means a lot. Come find me later, okay?
birthday.letter.romance.3: {{player}}:^^The whole valley should be celebrating you today—at least, that's how I feel.^^I've enclosed a small gift. Save a little time for me today.
birthday.letter.romance.4: To {{player}}:^^It took me several tries to write these few lines. Happy birthday. Days with you in them are always a little more special.^^The gift is inside. Come tell me if you like it.
birthday.letter.spouse.1: {{player}}:^^We see each other every day, but I still had to write this letter—I just want to see your face when you open it. It's your birthday again.^^The gift is under the letter. Come home before sunset.
birthday.letter.spouse.2: {{player}}:^^I want to remember every birthday I spend with you. Today is no different.^^There's a small gift in the envelope. The rest can wait until you're home.
birthday.letter.spouse.3: My {{player}}:^^Today is your day. Leave the farm work for now—I'll take care of things at home.^^Happy birthday. Keep the gift safe.
birthday.letter.spouse.4: To my dearest {{player}}:^^Another year with you—what a wonderful thing. Happy birthday!^^I'm sending a small gift ahead to start the day. Love you.

help.pets.title: Pet thoughts
help.kiss.title: Kisses and hugs
help.kiss.body:
At 10+ hearts after marriage, stand to your spouse's left or right and click them: two buttons pop up overhead, Chat and Kiss (Hug for a roommate). Pick with the mouse, a controller, or number keys. The first kiss each day raises friendship.
Hold Alt (LB on a controller) and click any villager for the vanilla interaction, skipping the AI.
Don't want the choice? Settings > General > AI, turn off "Choose chat or kiss when clicking your spouse".
help.talkFirst.title: I speak first
help.talkFirst.body:
Normally the villager says something first when you click them. With "I speak first" on, the dialogue box starts empty and waits for you.
You can also switch in the dialogue box: "Let them speak first" has them open this time; the "I'll speak first next time" toggle at the top right decides from then on.
When they have something to say, like a first meeting or the end of a story, they still speak first.
Settings > General > AI > I speak first.
help.pets.body:
When your pet is near you, a gray bubble sometimes pops up over its head with what it's thinking: hungry, wants pets, curious about something in the grass...
It's just talking to itself; you can't chat with pets yet, and clicking a pet still pets it.
Settings > Home > Pets: turn it off, or adjust lines per day and how often it happens.
help.kids.title: Talking with kids
help.kids.body:
Once a kid can walk, the first time you click them each day opens a dialogue box for a short chat. Kids talk like kids and won't discuss grown-up things like romance or money.
Write a character card for your kid: Settings > Setup > Villager character cards; kids are listed first, and you can write their personality, looks and way of talking.
Settings > Home > Kids: off / one line / chat.
help.runaway.title: Kids running off
help.runaway.body:
Some mornings a kid sneaks out onto the farm to hide and play. Your spouse will tell you (or message you if you're away).
How to find them: get close and you'll hear giggling, there are little footprints on the ground, and your spouse tells you the rough direction every two hours. Click the kid when you find them to bring them home, and your spouse will be relieved.
If they're still missing by evening, your spouse brings them back but will be in a worse mood.
Settings > Home > Kids: turn it off or adjust the chance.
help.mart.title: Farmer's Mart: where to build it and how to run it
help.compete.title: Competition and confrontations
help.compete.body:
The better your shop does, the worse Pierre's and JojaMart do: Normal > Struggling > Losing money > Closed for restructuring. When business is bad they shorten their hours and post a notice, but seeds are always available; this only affects AI Stardew Valley's own economy, not the vanilla story.
Once they're losing money, a shopkeeper may storm into your shop. You can reason with them (type your own argument), back down (raise prices 20% for a week), or fight (one punch like a vanilla cutscene; they stagger back and leave, nobody is hurt, but the mayor fines you, friendship drops a lot, and it makes the weekly paper).
Don't want fights? Turn off "Allow fighting" in Settings > Farmer's Mart. In Phone > Farmer's Mart you can invest in a rival; once invested you stop competing.
help.stolen.title: Stolen goods and staff
help.spouse.title: Spouse's daily plan
help.spouse.body:
After marriage your spouse plans their day every morning: watering, harvesting, caring for animals, refilling hay, collecting eggs, clearing the farm, tending the greenhouse and fish ponds; they also go to town to chat, shop, mind the mart, or play with the kids in the yard.
When you're on the farm you can see them out working; when you're away they still get it done. The harvest goes into the harvest chest.
Phone > Chores: see today's progress, collect the harvest, turn off a task, or ask them to do something for you. Saying "help me water" in a chat works too, and your spouse helps for free.
Settings > Home > Spouse's daily plan: how hard they help, where the harvest goes, daily spending. With low friendship they do less or nothing.
help.keys.title: Common keys
help.keys.body:
Hold Alt (LB on a controller) and click a villager: vanilla interaction.
Ctrl + Enter in the dialogue box: send.
See and change the other keys in Settings > Keys.

[Where to build] Go to Robin's carpenter shop (north of town, at the foot of the mountain), click the counter > Construct farm buildings > "Farmer's Mart" (15000g, 300 wood, 200 stone), place it in an open spot on the farm; it's done in two days, enter through the front door. [Inside] Laid out like Pierre's: counter and register at the top left, two white shelves, a glass fridge, a wooden cabinet and a sale bin already in place, and the big chest at the bottom right is the stockroom. For more shelves (also warmers and narrow shelves), buy them at Robin's.
[Stocking] Click a shelf while holding an item to put it up; click a shelf empty-handed to open the shelf window: your backpack is below, click an item to stock it (right-click puts just one), click a slot to change the price or take it down. Each shelf takes different goods: fish, eggs and milk spoil slower in the fridge, cooked food goes in the warmer, and the sale bin is the most eye-catching.
[Freshness] Counted from the day it's stocked: same day > fresh > normal > expiring > expired. Hardly anyone buys expired goods, and they get bad reviews. Minerals, artisan goods and artifacts don't spoil.
[Opening hours] 9:00 - 17:00 by default. While you're in the shop, villagers come in, pick goods and line up at the counter; click the counter to start checkout: scan items into the bag one by one, then make change with coins. Fast and correct earns tips. If nobody runs the register for too long, customers put things down and leave. When you're away it still sells; the money goes into the cashbox, click the counter to take it out.
[Running it] Phone > Farmer's Mart: pick a shop type (which goods you focus on), check today's market (what's in demand), order stock (arrives in the stockroom tomorrow morning), put up posters, set the display window, shout, hire staff (cashier / stocker / greeter, 7 or 28 days), read reviews.
[Competition] The better you sell, the worse Pierre and Joja do: struggling, losing money, even closed for restructuring (only AI Stardew Valley's economy; seeds are always available). Once they're losing money they may come to confront you.
[Note] If you sell stolen items in the shop, the owner and people who know them may recognize them.

help.stolen.body2:
Stolen items can go on the shelves too, and buyers occasionally recognize them (not often): the owner is most likely to, family and close friends next, passers-by rarely; the pricier it is, or the more suspiciously cheap, the easier it is to give yourself away, and the longer it sits the harder it is to recognize.
[Once recognized] The item is taken without payment, the mayor fines you (5× its value, 300-3000g), and a letter comes the next day. Whoever recognized it reacts on the spot by temperament: hot-tempered ones rant and rave, cold ones say one cutting thing and ignore you from then on, soft-hearted ones are so hurt they nearly cry, sharp-tongued ones mock you mercilessly. Friendship and mood both drop; the owner will later come to have it out with you, and Pierre and the nosy types will come to laugh at you; word spreads around town, it makes the weekly paper, and the shop's reputation suffers.
[Worse each time in a season] 2nd time: double fine and 3 days closed for restructuring; 3rd time on: triple fine, all stolen goods confiscated, closed 7 days, and you're taken away (to jail with Law and Order installed, otherwise the mayor escorts you home), ending the day. Resets each season. In Settings > Farmer's Mart you can turn off "Stolen goods may be recognized", and in Settings > Consequences you can turn off just being taken away.
Staff: Phone > Farmer's Mart > Staff, up to three, needs 4+ hearts. The cashier stands behind the counter and rings people up for you; the stocker removes expired items and restocks from the stockroom at 9, 12 and 3; the greeter says hi at the door for better reviews. Contracts are 7 or 28 days (28 days is a bit cheaper per day) and can be renewed. Wages are paid each night, taken from the cashbox first.

help.consequences.title: Consequences of misdeeds
help.consequences.body:
When you wrong someone, on top of the usual consequences (lost friendship, a few words), repeat offenses in the same season get worse; it resets each season.
[Standing people up] Agreed to meet and didn't show: they count it as breaking your word and their mood drops; the second time it gets around; the third time they won't meet with you this week.
[Not doing what you promised] Favors and requests that expire undone: counts as breaking your word, friendship drops a little; the second time it gets around and people say you're unreliable.
[Not paying debts] Loans and tabs at Gus's not repaid on time: a letter from the mayor; the second time it gets around; from the third time nobody will lend you money for two weeks and Gus won't run a tab.
[Fighting in your shop] Fighting when confronted: second time, double fine and a letter from the mayor; third time, you're taken away and the day ends.
[Caught stealing] With Stardew Thief installed, getting caught in the act repeatedly gets around, and the third time the mayor writes (fines and jail are still handled by Stardew Thief).
[Digging through trash] Repeatedly digging through someone's trash can in the same season: the owner writes to you, and by the third time people start giving you a nickname.
[Flirting in front of your partner] Flirting with someone right in front of your partner or spouse: they'll confront you and be hurt for days, with friendship and mood dropping; your spouse won't help with farm chores for a few days.
Each one can be turned off separately in Settings > Consequences; "Repeat offenders get taken away" is there too.

help.life.title: Villagers' own lives
help.life.body:
Villagers have things they want to achieve too: Haley wants to hold a photo exhibition, Sam's band wants its first gig, Robin wants to build a pavilion in town... A few are working on theirs at once (3 by default), each may take a step forward every week, and progress turns into gossip, makes the weekly paper, and comes up in chats.
[Helping] At some steps a villager asks you to find something (shown in the quest log). Bring it and their dream comes true sooner.
[Achieved] The villager writes to invite you. Go to the place in that week at the time in the letter to see an ending scene, and a picture is tucked into your diary. Some change jobs afterward, and the ledger and chats change with them.
[Romance] Two villagers with a secret crush may start dating and go on a date one evening a week (they give way if it clashes with your meetups or farm help). After a while they may get engaged, with a wedding on the town square a week later (go to town between 9 AM and 4 PM to see it); after marrying they still live where they did. Engaged and married couples are drawn together in the family tree. They may also break up. Villagers you are courting, dating or married to won't date anyone else; if you start dating one of a couple, that couple splits up.
Settings > Town life > Villagers' lives: main switch, how many at once, weddings, job changes. Romance between villagers also depends on "Villagers may develop feelings for each other".

help.multiplayer.title: Playing together online
help.multiplayer.body:
[How to use it] Everyone just installs the same version of AI Stardew Valley. The host computes everything for the village: gossip, the relationship web, villagers' lives, the weekly paper, today's moods, the villager ledger and the commission board, and farmhands automatically stay in sync with the host. If versions differ, farmhands see a notice, and their features stay local to them without syncing to the host.
[What farmhands can do] Chat with villagers (what you talk about turns into village gossip at night, and villagers know what other farmers talked to them about today); during face-to-face chats, arrange meetups with villagers or ask them to help on the farm (the host's side walks the villager over, and friendship, refunds and notices apply to you; arranging by message is still host-only); take commissions, hire villagers for errands, and borrow and repay money on the phone; if married, your spouse also plans their own day and puts what they collect into your own harvest chest.
[Each to their own] Consequences of misdeeds fall on whoever did it: fines come out of their money (out of everyone's money with a shared wallet), and letters and being taken away apply only to them. Letters, diaries and what villagers think of you are each player's own.
[Still host-only] The Farmer's Mart, arranging meetups by phone message, and kids running off.
[Split screen] When two people play split-screen on one computer, the second screen can't use features that need to sync with the host.
help.trouble.title: When something goes wrong
help.trouble.body:
If villagers stop talking, say strange things, or a feature doesn't respond:
[Self-check] Settings > Common > AI Status > Self-check (or type aisv_selfcheck in the SMAPI window). It checks whether the AI answers, whether your save data can be read, whether all asset files are there, conflicts with other mods, and the current state of each feature, and shows the result under the button after a few seconds.
[Reporting a problem] The full result is written to Mods/AIStardewValley/debug/selfcheck.txt with keys masked. Send it together with your SMAPI log.
[Test connection] The "Test connection" button on the same page just tries the AI once: does it connect, and how long does it take.
help.growing.title: Kids growing up
help.growing.body:
After learning to walk, kids keep growing: by default they reach school age two seasons later and become teens a year after that (change the pace or turn it off in Settings > Home > Kids). The day they grow up they look different, get a portrait in chats, and talk in longer, more age-appropriate ways; the first time they see you they run over to say something, and your spouse writes you a letter.
Their personality depends on how you spend time with them: chatting and playing often makes them lively, rarely paying attention makes them quiet, often watching class makes them curious, always finding them quickly makes them clingy, and taking a long time to find them makes them independent and mischievous. The day they grow up, a description of who they are now is written from these; if the character card sets a personality, the card wins.
School: on Penny's class days (Tuesday, Wednesday and Friday mornings in vanilla), school-age kids go to the museum for class with Jas and Vincent and come home at 2 PM; drop by the classroom and your kid will be thrilled, and Penny will mention how they're doing when you chat.
Teens: on weekends (when it isn't raining) they hang around town from 10 AM to 4 PM; when your spouse is minding the kids, teens help water a few tiles. Teens no longer run off.
Multiplayer: the host advances kids' stages so everyone sees the same thing; personality, the grow-up lines and letters are on the parent's own side.

help.meetup.title: Meetups and walking with you
help.meetup.body:
During chats, villagers may invite you to meet at a certain place and time on a certain day. If you accept, just be there when the time comes.
[Coming up to you] At the appointed time, if you're on the same map, they'll see you, come up to you, and speak first about the plans you made; then you can respond.
[Coming inside to find you] If you're more than twenty minutes late and you're in a nearby building, they'll open the door and come in to find you. They'll only enter your house at 4 hearts or higher (unless they're your spouse or partner); otherwise they'll wait outside.
[Walking with you] After you meet, they'll follow you for about two hours (until 10 PM at the latest), across maps too, and occasionally say something along the way. They won't enter the mines, casino, or changing rooms, and will say goodbye when you go there. Phone > Today, tap "That's all for today" to send them home early.
[Similar events] If a debt is due and unpaid, the lender will come to you in person to collect. Hired helpers will come over to greet you when they arrive. Villagers with something on their mind will follow you inside when you enter a building.
If you make a meetup and don't show up, it counts as standing them up. Settings > World: Walk with you after meeting, Come inside to find you.
